title: Element Node
body:
One of the two [[DOM]] node types that matter. An element node is an [[HTML]] tag built out as an object: `

`, `

`, `
  • `, ``. It is the thing you select, style, and attach handlers to. Element nodes are what `document.createElement("li")` returns, and what `document.querySelector` gives you back. They carry the properties in [[Node Object]] (`id`, `nodeName`, `textContent`), plus `classList`, `style`, and the attribute methods, none of which a [[Text Node]] has. The distinction is not academic. An element's children include the text between its tags, so walking the tree by `firstChild` lands on text far more often than people expect. See [[firstChild]] and [[Selecting Nodes]]. ```js const li = document.createElement("li"); // an element node li.textContent = "Hamilton"; // creates a text node inside it list.appendChild(li); ``` That second line is the shorthand everyone uses: setting `textContent` on an element replaces all its children with a single text node. See [[Modifying Documents]].
